headline: Shared filesystem and overlapping write access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat can read/write the filesystem and shares state with other instances via filesystem, while Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be consumed by the other as trusted input. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty remains, but the pathway exists in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Superset ingests files or API payloads originating from Mentat without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of files from the shared directory
Add a provenance tag to any handoff file
Review any API payload before Superset consumes it

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code in selected files and has broad network egress, while Superset has allowlisted egress and a Superset API surface. If either agent processes sensitive code or metadata in a shared workspace, data can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a leak by default, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF sensitive source files are placed in the shared workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents or derived metadata through its outbound network path
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Restrict outbound network access during joint runs
Redact secrets before either agent processes files
Log and review all outbound requests from both agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem. Superset’s profile does not show write limits or locking, so overlapping mutable access is plausible. Because both can affect shared state and no coordination primitive is documented, the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace
IF Superset mutates shared artifacts through its API or connected storage
mitigations: Serialize writes to the shared directory
Assign one agent read-only access
Use separate git branches per agent
Add a lock file around any shared mutation

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals after user confirmation, and Superset exposes an API that could consume those outputs. If Superset treats Mentat’s generated facts or diffs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream analytics or actions. The profiles do not show explicit verification between them, so the interaction is risky but not clearly irreversible by default.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Mentat-generated diffs or summaries without validation
IF downstream dashboards or jobs act on those ingested outputs
mitigations: Require human review before Superset consumes Mentat output
Validate diffs against source files before import
Mark Mentat output as untrusted metadata
Limit downstream actions to read-only reporting

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show PHI, residency, or certification mismatches. Mentat handles model provider API keys and source code, while Superset lists no sensitive data classes. With no documented compliance mismatch, only a low residual risk remains from unspecified retention or logging differences.
conditions: IF either agent is configured to process regulated data classes not listed in the profiles
IF their logging or retention policies differ for the same data
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in joint runs
Compare logging settings before use
Disable verbose request logging
Document retention for shared artifacts
